name: Recruit company drivers
summary: Driver recruiters take each application from job boards, the careers page and driving schools, screen it against the insurer's hiring standard, pull the driver abstract, verify three years of previous driving employment and, for cross-border drivers, run the US drug and alcohol checks. Truckload and LTL managers interview the survivors, the recruiting manager approves the hire and the candidate goes to road testing. About one application in eight becomes a candidate. The process is slow because applicants are hard to reach, previous employers answer late or not at all, and in 2021 and 2022 candidates took competing offers while files were still open.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian LTL and truckload carrier of about 3,000 employees and 1,210 company drivers with a central driver recruiting team in its safety department.
baseline.notes: About 450 applications a month lead to about 55 qualified candidates and, after road tests, about 45 company driver hires. About 65% of hires go to truckload and 35% to LTL; about a third of candidates will run into the US.

trigger: A driver applicant or driving-school graduate submits an application through the careers page, a job board or a school referral.
end_state: The candidate has accepted a conditional offer and is booked for a road test and orientation, or the application is declined or withdrawn.

volume.seasonality: Applications fall in December and rise in January to March and again in late summer before the autumn LTL peak; 2020 Q2 was low during lockdowns and 2021-2022 were high.

evidence.note: Organisation process map volume. About 500 company hires a year follow from 13% LTL and 90% large truckload US turnover scaled down for Canada; about one hire per ten applications is the author's estimate.

surge.cause: Hiring drives before the autumn LTL peak and after spring driving-school graduations

evidence.note: Carriers run advertising and referral-bonus campaigns before peak; size is the author's estimate.
Org file headcount of 14; about 3 FTE go to advertising, job fairs, school visits and owner-operator leads outside this per-application process. Author's estimate.
Hire approvals and exception calls with the insurer; rest of the role is campaign planning and reporting. Author's estimate.
Truckload driver managers interview about 30 candidates a month. Not listed for this process in the org file. Author's estimate.
Terminal managers interview LTL candidates for their own terminals. Not listed for this process in the org file. Author's estimate.

systems.name: Email, phone system and contact centre software
Safety management system (driver files, collisions, roadside inspections)

steps.name: Receive application in the applicant tracking system
steps.description: The applicant tracking system receives an online application from the careers page, a job board or a driving-school referral, applies knock-out questions (licence class, years of experience, home location) and emails an automatic acknowledgement. It places the application in the recruiter queue for the applicant's home region.

error.defect_description: Knock-out answers wrong or the application routed to the wrong region.

evidence.note: Driver applicant tracking systems were standard at mid-size and large carriers by 2019; author's knowledge.

steps.name: Screen application against hiring minimums
steps.description: A driver recruiter opens the application and compares it with the hiring standard for the opening: licence class (AZ or Class 1), years of verifiable experience, recent job changes, home location against the terminal or lane, and willingness to cross the border. The recruiter decides to call the applicant, decline, or merge a duplicate.

error.defect_description: A qualified applicant declined on a misread work history.

next.condition: below minimum experience, wrong licence or outside hiring area
duplicate application or applicant already in process

evidence.note: Most carriers required at least one year's experience for insurance reasons; screening split is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Phone-screen the applicant
steps.description: The recruiter calls the applicant, often several times, to confirm experience, equipment driven, home time expectations, pay and any collisions or tickets the applicant volunteers. The recruiter explains the lane, pay per mile or hour and benefits and records notes in the tracking system.

next.condition: cannot be reached or no longer interested

evidence.note: Call attempts and contact rates are the author's estimate; applicants in 2021 applied to several carriers at once (Trucking HR Canada vacancy data show a tight market).

steps.name: Applicant completes full application and consents
steps.description: The applicant fills in the full driver application with employment history, licences, collisions and convictions, and signs consents for the driver abstract, criminal record check and previous-employer safety history inquiry. Cross-border candidates add passport, FAST card or visa details.

evidence.note: Consent to previous-employer safety history inquiries is required for US-bound drivers under 49 CFR 391.23; completion rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Order driver abstract and commercial record
steps.description: The recruiter orders the provincial driver abstract (three years or more) and, where the applicant has run their own authority, the commercial operator record, through the ministry or an abstract service. The recruiter attaches the order to the application.

control.basis: 49 CFR 391.23(a)(1) driving record inquiry for drivers operating into the US; insurer hiring standard for domestic drivers

evidence.note: Driving record from each licensing authority of the past 3 years is required for US-bound drivers; Canadian insurers ask for the same.

steps.name: Wait for abstract
steps.description: The ministry or abstract service returns the abstract. Ontario abstracts ordered online come back the same day; Quebec, out-of-province and US records can take several days.

evidence.note: Turnaround by jurisdiction is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review abstract against insurer hiring standard
steps.description: The recruiter reads the abstract and counts demerit points, moving violations, at-fault collisions and suspensions in the look-back period, and compares them with the insurer's hiring grid. Borderline records are flagged for the recruiting manager.

error.defect_description: A conviction or collision missed in a long abstract.

evidence.note: Insurer-driven hiring standards described by brokers and carriers; failure share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Send previous-employer verification requests
steps.description: The recruiter emails or faxes each driving employer of the past three years a verification form asking for dates, equipment, collisions, reason for leaving and, for US-regulated employers, drug and alcohol history. Gaps over 30 days are noted for the applicant to explain.

control.basis: 49 CFR 391.23(a)(2) and (e) previous-employer safety performance history inquiry

evidence.note: Three-year safety performance history inquiry with drug and alcohol history, and 30 days for previous employers to respond.

steps.name: Order criminal record check and verify border documents
steps.description: While verifications are out, the recruiter orders a criminal record check through a screening vendor and checks passport, FAST card or US visa for cross-border openings. A record that bars US entry ends a cross-border candidacy but may leave a domestic opening.

evidence.note: Criminal record checks and border-document checks are common practice for cross-border fleets; author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for previous-employer responses and background results
steps.description: Previous employers return the verification forms and the vendor returns the criminal record check. Large carriers answer within days; small fleets and closed companies often do not answer at all.

evidence.note: Previous employers have 30 days to respond under 49 CFR 391.23(g); typical delays are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Chase missing verifications
steps.description: The recruiter phones and re-faxes the employers that have not answered, asks the applicant to nudge former supervisors, and records each attempt as a documented good-faith effort when no answer comes.

next.condition: responses received or good-faith effort documented

evidence.note: Carriers must document good-faith efforts when previous employers do not respond.

steps.name: Review verifications and background results
steps.description: The recruiter compares employer answers with the dates and collisions the applicant declared, reads the background result, and decides whether the candidate goes forward and to which fleet (cross-border truckload, domestic truckload or LTL).

error.defect_description: A discrepancy between declared and verified employment missed.

next.condition: cross-border candidate needs drug and alcohol screening
undisclosed collisions, falsified history or record bars the opening

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Run Clearinghouse query and book drug test
steps.description: For drivers who will run into the US, the recruiter obtains the driver's consent, runs the pre-employment full query of the FMCSA Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse (from January 2020) and books a pre-employment drug test at a collection site near the applicant.

control.basis: 49 CFR 382.701 pre-employment Clearinghouse query and 382.301 pre-employment testing

evidence.note: Pre-employment full query required before a driver performs safety-sensitive functions.

steps.name: Applicant attends drug test and result is reported
steps.description: The applicant goes to the collection site, the laboratory tests the specimen and the medical review officer reports the result to the carrier, usually two to three business days later.

evidence.note: Laboratory turnaround and positive rate are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Truckload driver manager interviews candidate
steps.description: A truckload driver manager meets or calls the candidate to explain lanes, home time, equipment and dispatch practice, and judges fit with the fleet. The driver manager records a hire or no-hire recommendation.

evidence.note: Operations managers commonly meet candidates before an offer; author's estimate.

steps.name: Terminal manager interviews LTL candidate
steps.description: The terminal manager of the hiring terminal interviews the candidate in person, walks the yard and docks, explains city or linehaul runs, seniority and union rules where they apply, and records a recommendation.

evidence.note: Terminal managers hire for their own terminals at LTL carriers; author's estimate.

steps.name: Compile candidate file and recommend hire
steps.description: The recruiter assembles the application, abstract, verifications, background result, drug test result and interview notes into one candidate file, notes any exceptions to the hiring standard and sends it to the recruiting manager.

error.defect_description: A document missing from the file.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Recruiting manager approves hire
steps.description: The driver recruiting manager reviews the file, checks that every required record is present and decides exceptions to the insurer standard, which may need the insurer's agreement. The manager approves, declines or sends the file back for a missing item.

control.basis: Insurer hiring standard and company hiring policy: second-person approval of driver hires

evidence.note: Manager sign-off and insurer exception approval are common practice; author's estimate.

steps.name: Re-key candidate into safety and HR systems
steps.description: Because the tracking system is not linked to the safety system or the HR system, the recruiter re-types the candidate's name, licence, abstract date, medical expiry and verifications into the safety system and sends the HR coordinator a new-hire request.

error.defect_description: Licence number or expiry date mistyped.

evidence.note: Separate tracking, safety and HR systems were common in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Make conditional offer and book road test
steps.description: The recruiter phones the candidate with a conditional offer subject to the road test and file completion, books the road test and the next orientation class, and passes the candidate to onboarding.

evidence.note: Offer losses to competing carriers in the tight 2021-2022 market (only 12.2% of vacancies filled within 15 days); share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Send decline and close application
steps.description: The recruiter selects a decline reason in the tracking system, which sends a standard decline email, and keeps the file for the retention period. Recruiters often batch declines once or twice a week.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Previous employer never answers
exceptions.description: A closed or small former employer never returns the verification; the recruiter documents good-faith efforts and the manager decides whether to proceed.

exceptions.name: Insurer exception
exceptions.description: A candidate with less experience or a marginal abstract needs the insurer's written agreement before the manager can approve.

exceptions.name: Cross-border candidate with a record barring US entry
exceptions.description: The background check shows a record that bars US entry; the candidate is offered a domestic opening or declined.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from application received to decline, withdrawal or accepted conditional offer
benchmarks.population: All driver applications at a mid-size Canadian carrier, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Most applications are declined or drop out within a few days; qualified candidates take two to four weeks because of previous-employer verifications and interviews. Author's estimate; no published Canadian figure found.

benchmarks.population: Canadian truck driver vacancies, Q3 2021 (34.5% in Q2 2021)
Canadian truck driver vacancies, Q3 2021 (20.8% in Q2 2021)

evidence.note: US figures; Canadian turnover assumed lower (about 50% truckload, 15% LTL) in the organisation file.

pain_points.description: Applicants apply to several carriers at once and are hard to reach; about a quarter of phone screens never happen.

evidence.note: Author's estimate, consistent with the record vacancy levels of 2021.

pain_points.description: Previous-employer verifications take days to weeks and often need chasing; the file cannot close until responses or good-faith efforts are documented.

evidence.note: 30-day response window and good-faith documentation rule.

pain_points.description: Candidate data is typed again into the safety and HR systems, which introduces licence and expiry date errors.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: In the 2021-2022 driver shortage, candidates accepted faster competing offers while files waited for verifications, interviews and approval.

evidence.note: Only 12.2% of driver vacancies were filled within 15 days in Q3 2021.

sources.title: Turnover Remained Unchanged at Large Truckload Fleets in Fourth Quarter
sources.supports: US annualized driver turnover in 2020: large truckload fleets 90% (92% in Q4), small truckload 69%, LTL 13% (12% in Q4).

sources.title: Canadian truck driver vacancies surge to record levels: Report
sources.publisher: Trucknews.com (reporting Trucking HR Canada labour market data)
sources.supports: 22,990 vacant truck driver jobs in Q3 2021, up 20% from Q2; 44.3% vacant for more than 90 days (34.5% in Q2); only 12.2% filled within 15 days (20.8% in Q2); truck transportation vacancy rate 8% against 5.4% for all sectors; Ontario 6,080 vacancies; CTA expected 12,000 to 16,000 drivers could leave cross-border work under the vaccine mandate.

sources.title: New drivers traverse difficult road to employment
sources.supports: Most carriers require at least one year's experience, mainly because of insurance; carriers with fleet policies can hire newly licensed drivers if they run onboarding, finishing or mentoring programs; carriers prefer Canadian experience for cross-border work; US visa waits delay new drivers' cross-border eligibility.

sources.title: 49 CFR 391.23 Investigation and inquiries
sources.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
sources.supports: Within 30 days of employment beginning, obtain the driving record from every licensing authority of the past 3 years and investigate the driver's safety performance history with DOT-regulated employers of the past 3 years, including drug and alcohol violations, with the driver's written consent; previous employers must respond within 30 days; document good-faith efforts when they do not.

sources.title: 49 CFR 382.701 Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse
sources.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
sources.supports: Employers must not use a driver subject to testing in safety-sensitive functions without first conducting a pre-employment full query of the Clearinghouse with the driver's consent, and must query at least once a year.

assumptions: US rules (49 CFR 391 and 382) apply to drivers who will operate into the US, about a third of candidates; domestic-only candidates follow the insurer's standard, which asks for the same abstract and employment checks but no drug test.

Funnel: 48% pass the first screen, 55% of those pass the phone screen, 85% complete the full application, 83% pass the abstract, 92% pass verifications, about 86% pass interviews and drug tests, 93% are approved and 88% accept the offer: about 12% of applications become qualified candidates (about 55 a month).
Interview step roles: driver-manager for truckload and terminal-manager for LTL. The organisation file lists only the recruiter and recruiting manager for this process.
Recruiters work office hours; waits include evenings and weekends.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (wage x 1.35 for salaried office staff, x 1.30 for hourly staff).

Staffing: the roles state about 12 FTE while hands-on time times 450 applications implies about 4.5 FTE. The gap is lead handling not counted as applications (calls and partial web leads, often several times the application count), job fairs, school visits, advertising and follow-up with candidates who are not yet ready; if those are excluded, about 6 to 8 recruiters would cover this volume.
Simulated median cycle time is short because most applications end at the first screens; candidates who reach an offer take about two to four weeks.
